behaviors: Complete parser and all four legacy test functions reviewed. ECMAScript whitespace, optional leading question mark, first colon split, first occurrence ordering, required/default flags and host-owned cwd/projectCwd exclusions use the existing shared Rust parser.

The canonical18-case corpus now explicitly names the Rust owner and enforces an executed-case floor through the shared nondiscardable Tally, in addition to enumeration and exact ordered outputs. No expected case value changed.

Actual Hub/Client library.save and library.list calls prove dispatch params are derived from the stored body on both responses, ordinary prompt rows omit params, caller-forged derived params are never persisted, and both host automatic variables are excluded.

Filters are proved against the real unfiltered listing: kind filtering preserves relative order; ID filtering selects one; kind and ID are ANDed; empty filters mean no filter; missing IDs return empty; unknown kinds fail. The persisted frontmatter is read and parsed to prove no params key was written.
intentionalChanges: Rust keeps the explicit empty default property specified by the normative TypeScript/JSON corpus; Go struct omitempty omitted that property on wire while comparing it as the same empty string in its typed tests.

The shared Rust module also renders validated templates after host context is resolved. This record ports the former parser/discovery responsibility; full launch/worktree ownership retains its separate evidence.
